Pinned at its FIRST HONEST READING, 2026-09-01 (lane E8-GATES). ROWS, NEVER A COUNT.
The gate compares NAMES in BOTH directions and exits 3 on either difference.
WHAT THESE ROWS ARE — the spec-§20 failure, measured at the seam where it happens.
The E1bc declarative loader (rulepacks/declarative/deriveC58Contract.ts) takes the
Barcelona 20a migration pilot, whose 57 of 66 rules are stamped
derivation: AI_EXTRACTED / confidence.tier 4 / valueLocation: in-document-text, and
emits a C58 contract whose every field reads fieldProvenance: ordinance-pdf —
which C58 §1.6 defines as A HUMAN TRANSCRIBED A LEGAL PDF ORDINANCE — at
defaultConfidence: estimated-ruleset, two rungs above pipeline-extracted-unverified.
Arm E then solves that derived contract through the REAL computeBuildableEnvelope
and reads estimated-ruleset back off nine buildable envelopes. That is the exact
sentence the wave exists to forbid: an AI-extracted number reaching a
buildable-envelope calculation UNLABELLED.
THE GATE DOES NOT DECIDE WHICH SIDE IS WRONG, AND MUST NOT. Two readings are
available and only a curator can pick: either the rules are honestly stamped
AI_EXTRACTED and the pack labels launder them, or the migration over-stamped a
human-curated transcription as AI_EXTRACTED. What the gate asserts is that the two
axes CONTRADICT EACH OTHER, which is true either way.
NOT YET LIVE. The document is exported from the barrel but registered in NO
rule-pack registry: no parcel resolves through it today, and only
declarativeGoldenParity.test.ts drives it. It goes live as-is the day the
hand-written TS pack is retired — which is why the row is pinned before then.
EXIT CONDITION: make the LABELS agree with the CLAIMS. Either stamp the migrated
rules with the derivation that is actually true, or carry the machine tier through
to the pack default and per-field flags. Both are honest.
NOT by deleting rows and NOT by relaxing the auditor.
